items.question: ___ are loyal animals. (in general)
explanations: 'The dogs' points to specific dogs, not dogs in general.
Correct! General plurals take no article: 'Dogs are loyal animals'.
'A dog' is one dog, not dogs in general.
'The dog' means one specific dog.

items.question: ___ is essential for life. (in general)
explanations: 'The water' would mean specific water.
'A water' means one portion, not water in general.
Correct! Uncountables in general take no article: 'Water is essential'.

items.question: I usually have ___ at eight.
explanations: 'A breakfast' only works when described (a big breakfast).
'The breakfast' would need a specific one.
Correct! Meals take no article: 'have breakfast'.

items.question: The children go to ___ by bus.
explanations: 'The school' means the building, changing the meaning.
'A school' would mean any school.
Correct! 'Go to school' (as students) takes no article.

items.question: ___ lives in ___ . (a person and a country)
explanations: Names take no article, even if Catalan says 'la Sara'.
'Italy' takes no 'the' (unlike the USA).
Correct! 'Sara lives in Italy' — no article with names or most countries.

items.question: ___ can't buy happiness.
explanations: 'Money' is uncountable: it has no plural.
Correct! Uncountable in general: 'Money can't buy happiness'.
'The money' would be specific money.

items.question: She's learning ___ at university.
explanations: 'The Japanese' would mean the Japanese people.
Languages have no plural form here.
Correct! Languages take no article: 'learning Japanese'.

items.question: Choose the correct version of: 'I go to the bed at eleven.'
options: I go to a bed at eleven.
I go to bed at eleven.
explanations: 'A bed' changes it to a random bed.
'Go to the bed' wrongly adds 'the'.
Correct! The fixed phrase is 'go to bed' — no article.

items.question: Which sentence talks about music IN GENERAL?
explanations: 'The music' means specific music (e.g. at a party).
Correct! General uncountable: 'I love music' (no article).
'Music' is uncountable: it has no plural.

items.question: When do you use the zero article (no article)?
options: With a singular countable first mention.
explanations: Correct! General plurals and uncountables take no article.
A specific, known noun takes 'the'.
A first-mention singular countable takes a/an.
Superlatives take 'the'.

items.question: The money can't buy happiness.
items.explanation: We mean money in general, so no article.

items.question: We go to the bed at eleven.
answers: We go to bed at eleven
items.explanation: 'Go to bed' is a fixed phrase with no article.

items.question: I usually go to work ___ car.
items.explanation: 'By car' is a fixed phrase with no article.

common.why: We say 'by car' with no article. 'In my car' needs 'my'.
